localisation.note: geometric sanity check, near-exact by construction — not the achievement

verdict: Partner-screening for LOSS decomposes into two separable jobs, and the honest result is that the node does the first for free and needs its full ΔΔG model for the second. LOCALISATION — 'which partner's interface is this residue on' — is near-EXACT (top-1 98% vs 25% random), but that is because it is pure geometry / near-field STRUCTURE, the recoverable regime; it is a reliable layer, not a hard prediction. MAGNITUDE — 'how much does THIS substitution change binding' — is the real problem, and the key honest finding is that the localisation/burial score ALONE does NOT predict it: across mixed substitutions burial vs measured |ΔΔG| is r -0.01 (~0), because burial ignores what you mutate TO. Fix the substitution (X->Ala) and the on-target signal reappears (r 0.51); and burial cleanly separates the FUNCTIONAL interface — SKEMPI core residues (burial 1, measured |ΔΔG| 1.97) from surface ones (burial 0, |ΔΔG| 0.27). So the usable screen is LOCALISATION (structure, exact) x MAGNITUDE (the full ΔΔG model, Pearson ~0.52) — flag 'this mutation is on partner P's interface AND is predicted to cost a lot' => LOSS of P, and predict ~no effect on partners the residue never touches. GAIN, stated plainly: affinity-increasing mutations are real (6% of SKEMPI) and the full model can score them at an existing interface, but a NOVEL emergent partner is NOT something this pipeline can claim — that is the dynamics-side problem (docking an unseen complex + experiment) the whole project keeps finding does not compose. Bottom line: a good LOSS/specificity screen, an honest NO on novel-partner discovery.
